question: The points $A(k,0)$, $B(0,k)$ and $C(1,1)$ form a triangle of area $\frac{3}{2}$ square units. Determine all real values of $k$.
explanation:
Determinant form of the area
The area condition is $$\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}k&0&1\\0&k&1\\1&1&1\end{vmatrix}\right|=\frac{3}{2}$$
Evaluation of the determinant
Expanding along the first row gives $$k(k-1)+(0-k)=k^2-2k$$ Therefore, $$|k^2-2k|=3$$
Positive case
If $k^2-2k=3$, then $$k^2-2k-3=0$$ Thus, $$(k-3)(k+1)=0$$ giving $k=3$ or $k=-1$.
Negative case
If $k^2-2k=-3$, then $k^2-2k+3=0$, whose discriminant is $4-12=-8<0$. Hence, it has no real solution.
Therefore, $k=3$ or $k=-1$.
